question: Should OpenClaw define a backend-neutral distributed job/scheduler ownership contract in core or plugin APIs, document Redis/BullMQ orchestration as external only, or defer the broad worker queue layer to narrower cron/session/runtime trackers?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but backend ownership, config shape, worker failure semantics, credential model, observability, and core-versus-plugin boundaries are maintainer product and architecture choices.

options.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
options.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, observability, and plugin/core ownership before landing backend-specific code.

options.title: Document External Pattern
options.body: Keep core single-process for now and document ScalyClaw/BullMQ-style orchestration as an external deployment or plugin pattern without adding core surfaces.

options.title: Defer To Narrow Trackers
options.body: Let cron HA, external session storage, and distributed runtime trackers settle first, then revisit whether a broader distributed worker layer is still needed.

recommendation.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
recommendation.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, observability, and plugin/core ownership before landing backend-specific code.
